article_title: Effectiveness of Problem-Based Learning versus Traditional Teaching Methods in Improving Acquisition of Radiographic Interpretation Skills among Dental Students-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
citation: Luke Alexander Maniangat, Mathew Simy, Kuriadom Sam Thomas, George Jeny Mary, Karobari Mohmed Isaqali, Marya Anand, Pawar Ajinkya Mansing. (2021). Effectiveness of Problem-Based Learning versus Traditional Teaching Methods in Improving Acquisition of Radiographic Interpretation Skills among Dental Students—A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. BioMed Research International. https://doi.org/10.1155/2021/9630285
title: Evidence pool of 13 studies (835 dental students) comparing PBL-type and traditional teaching in oral radiology
description: The review's quantitative base: 13 studies conducted in Australia, Brazil, Greece, India, North Carolina, South Korea, Sweden, and Toronto, of which eight were randomized controlled trials and five nonrandomized. "A total of 835 participants were part of the studies' analysis, with 411 in the problem-based learning group and 424 in the traditional teaching group." All participants were undergraduate dental students who already had basic theoretical knowledge of radiographic interpretation, with follow-up ranging from immediate assessment to about 8 months.
requirements: Studies had to report outcome variables for radiographic interpretation skills, knowledge, or satisfaction and include both an intervention and a comparison group
constraints: All participants already had basic theoretical knowledge about principles of radiographic interpretation; interventions were mainly short-term except one extending to 8 months
examples: Risk of bias assessment found only four studies with low risk; per AHRQ only two of eight RCTs showed good quality while five were of poor quality
key_sources: Luke Alexander Maniangat, Mathew Simy, Kuriadom Sam Thomas, George Jeny Mary, Karobari Mohmed Isaqali, Marya Anand, Pawar Ajinkya Mansing. (2021). Effectiveness of Problem-Based Learning versus Traditional Teaching Methods in Improving Acquisition of Radiographic Interpretation Skills among Dental Students—A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. article_title: Pilot study: the impact of simulation-based pediatric basic life support training on the performance of caregivers of children with Rett syndrome.
citation: Kocyigit S, Akgun-Dogan O, Hatirnaz Ng O, Alanay Y, Guven F. (2026). Pilot study: the impact of simulation-based pediatric basic life support training on the performance of caregivers of children with Rett syndrome. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09158-y
title: 13-item training evaluation questionnaire adapted from validated international tools
description: A paper-based 13-item questionnaire used to assess caregiver satisfaction with the simulation training. It was adapted from validated international tools and uses 5-point Likert-scale items (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree) addressing six domains: motivation and engagement, training focus, skill and confidence development, training duration and content clarity, effectiveness of teaching methods, and teamwork and communication.
constraints: The questionnaire was not independently validated in this caregiver population
target_learners: Simulation training participants, including lay caregivers
target_learning_goals: Evaluation of participant satisfaction, confidence, and perceived preparedness following simulation-based training
examples: The full questionnaire is provided in the article's Additional file
